transcript.text: my samsung washer dryer is making evrything smell damp/musty even after its washed, its gross. wot do i do

That musty smell is almost always a hygiene build-up inside the machine rather than a broken part, so the odds are good you can sort it yourself. Most likely causes, in order:
1. Mould and bacteria (biofilm) growing in the rubber door-seal folds, the detergent drawer, the pump filter or behind the drum. This builds up fastest with lots of cool or quick washes, liquid detergent and fabric softener.
2. Too much detergent or softener, which leaves a sticky residue the bacteria feed on. Keeping the door shut between washes makes it worse.
3. Clothes not quite dry at the end of a drying cycle, or left sitting damp in the drum. Either can smell musty even when the machine itself is clean.
4. Less likely, a drain smell from the standpipe or sink trap behind the machine. That smells sharp, like rotten eggs, rather than earthy. What to do (unplug the machine first):
1. Pull back the rubber door seal and look right into the folds, especially at the bottom. Black spots, slime or a fluffy gunk mean the seal is the main source. Wipe it out with a cloth and diluted washing-up liquid or a mould spray, then dry it. If the mould is soaked into the rubber, or the seal is torn, it may eventually need replacing, but clean it first.
2. Pull the detergent drawer right out and scrub it and the housing it slides into. Mould often hides up in the roof of that recess.
3. Clean the pump filter, the small round cap at the bottom front. Put towels down and have a shallow tray ready, because water will come out. Unscrew it slowly and clear any fluff or gunk. On a washer-dryer, drying fluff collects here, and a dirty filter smells.
4. Run an empty hot wash at 90°C with a washing-machine cleaner or a cup of soda crystals. If yours has a Drum Clean or self-clean programme, use that. If the smell is much better afterwards, it was biofilm. To stop it coming back:
• Leave the door and drawer ajar between washes.
• Use less detergent and go easy on softener.
• Do a 60°C wash now and then.
• Take laundry out as soon as it finishes.
• Repeat the maintenance wash about monthly. If it still smells after all that, the next things to look at are whether the drying cycle is fully drying the clothes and whether the drain plumbing is the source. To point you the right way: is it an earthy musty smell, or more like drains or rotten eggs? And is there any black mould or slime in the door-seal folds o
its a damp earthy smell, not drains or eggs. the door seal has black spots and grey sludge in the bottom fold, yuck. the drawer is slimy and black in the softener bit too

That settles it fairly clearly. Nothing is broken. The machine is simply seeding that smell back into every load. I'm confident this is the main cause, and it's very fixable. 1. Door seal: fold the bottom of the seal back and scoop out the sludge with kitchen roll first. Then spray the folds with a mould and mildew spray, leave it 10–15 minutes, scrub with an old toothbrush and wipe dry. Don't mix different cleaning products, especially anything with bleach. Some black spotting can stain the rubber permanently. That's only cosmetic if the smell goes. If the seal is split or the mould can't be shifted at all, a new seal is the long-term fix, but clean it properly first.
2. Drawer: pull it fully out and soak it in hot soapy water for 20 minutes. Many drawers have a small clip-in cap in the softener section that pulls off, so give underneath that a good scrub too. Then shine a torch into the empty drawer recess and scrub its roof and back, where the black stuff usually hides.
3. Pump filter: clean it as described before, with towels down and a tray ready. The sludge in the seal suggests it's probably grubby too.
4. Hot empty wash: run a 90°C cycle (or the drum-clean programme) with a machine cleaner or soda crystals. If the first run still smells a bit, a second run often finishes the job. Afterwards, wash one load and smell it. If it comes out fresh, it was the biofilm. If clean clothes still smell musty, the next suspect is laundry staying damp, either from the drying cycle not quite finishing or from clothes sitting in the drum. To stop it coming back, it helps to know how you normally wash. Do you mostly use 30–40°C or quick cycles, with liquid detergent and fabric softener, and does the door usually stay shut between washes?
yeah mostly 30 or even 20 degrees, with liquid detergent and loads of softener. and i shut the door straight away after a wash. never done the drum clean thing either

That explains it completely. Those four habits together are the perfect recipe for that smell, so it's very fixable. Here's why it happens. At 20–30°C nothing in the drum gets hot enough to kill mould or bacteria. Liquid detergents also don't contain the oxygen bleach that powders have, and that bleach is what normally keeps the machine clean. Fabric softener is waxy. Used generously, it coats the drum, the hidden outer tub and the drawer, and the mould feeds on it. That's why the softener section is the worst bit. Shutting the door straight away then traps the moisture, so it all grows between washes. With no hot or drum-clean wash ever run, there's probably a fair layer of gunk behind the drum you can't see. That's also why one deep clean may need a second hot run. 1. Use a biological powder or capsules with bleach for at least some washes, such as towels, bedding and anything grubby. You can keep liquid for colours and delicates. Even a mix makes a big difference.
2. Do a 60°C wash at least once a week. Towels, bed linen and underwear are ideal for it. Keep 20°C for lightly worn things only.
3. Cut the softener right back, to half the dose or less, and never fill past the MAX line. Better still, skip it on loads you're tumble drying in the machine, because drying softens them anyway.
4. Leave the door and the drawer open after every wash, and give the bottom fold of the seal a quick wipe dry with a cloth.
5. Run the drum clean programme (or an empty 90°C wash with cleaner or soda crystals) once a month. Many Samsung machines will remind you with a light or message when it's due.
6. Take the washing out as soon as it finishes. If the smell is gone after the clean, it was the build-up, and those habits will keep it away. In that case a new seal is the usual fix, though try the cleaning first. Let me know how the first load comes out after the deep clean.
